ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against Luxembourg's national list (CSSF/banque centrale), EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and Interpol notices. Enhanced due diligence mandatory for any PEP, family member or close associate of a PEP, regardless of country. Negative news and sanctions screening on a rolling 5-year look-back, with source documentation retained for 5 years post-cessation of business relationship.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_register_obligation: The RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) must be filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) within one month after incorporation. Report includes full name, DOB, nationality, residential address, and nature/extent of beneficial ownership. Effective 1 September 2020, access to the RBE is restricted to the Luxembourg financial intelligence unit (FIU) and other designated competent authorities; public access has been suspended following ECJ judgment C‑37/20.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_penalty_notice: Failure to file RBE within 1 month carries criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal entities and imprisonment for individuals, plus administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and suspension of director rights.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCSL), online via LBR (Luxembourg Business Registers) - https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in a Latin alphabet script; French, German, or Luxembourgish preferred; a name may also be in another language if written in Latin characters. The name must include 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the acronym 'SARL' (or 'S.à r.l.'). Any transliteration of a foreign name must be phonetically equivalent in Latin script and distinguishable from existing names. Use of Luxembourgish characters (ë, ä, ü) is permissible. The name must not violate public policy or morality, mislead as to activity, or be identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name or trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds / Fund (requires CSSF authorisation or specific fund regime)
État / State / Gouvernement / Government (misleading public entity)
Communauté européenne / European Community (protected EU insignia)
Université / University (requires Higher Education Ministry approval)
Avocat / Attorney (reserved to members of the Bar)
Auditeur / Auditor (reserved to approved statutory auditors)
Établissement à caractère public (suggests public body)
Kreditinstitut / Credit Institution (reserved under banking law)
Nacional, Federal, Authority, Royal, or any royal/state heraldic references
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected due to identity or similarity with an existing name, the incorporator may file a new name application after 30 days or immediately with a distinguishable variant. An administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of Justice (Ministère de la Justice) within 2 months of the rejection notice, under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce. The appeal must state legal arguments and documentary evidence of distinctiveness; where rejection is based on public policy grounds, an appeal lies to the Conseil d'État (Council of State) within 3 months. No separate extension of the 30-day reservation is available; re-filing after 30 days is required. A temporary reservation fee of EUR 30 covers two consecutive reservation attempts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office (siège social virtuel) is not permissible for a SARL. The SARL must have a real, physical registered office in Luxembourg that is accessible to the authorities and at which legal correspondence is served. However, a shared office or co-working space with a dedicated mailing address and meeting rooms may be acceptable if it constitutes a genuine administrative establishment and the company's statutory records are kept there. The registered office must be in the same municipality as the RCSL filing. The RCSL and tax office must be notified of any change within one month.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk 3D art outsourcing studio operating under ISIC 7490, the probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months is estimated at 15–20%, primarily arising from AML/CFT desk reviews of UBO declarations and possible visits by the Social Security Inspectorate (Inspection générale de la sécurité sociale) after hiring occurs. If the registered office is a known virtual office or co-working space, the likelihood increases to 30–40% because authorities may verify substantial substance. Maintain an occupied workspace, signage, business records, and staff presence during normal business hours to reduce risk.

stage_1.additional_professional_notes: Luxembourg imposes mandatory legal reserve of 5% of annual net profits until reaching 10% of subscribed capital. Minimum subscribed share capital for an SARL is EUR 12,000 (fully paid in at incorporation); for a single-member SARL no minimum share capital is required if it is insolvent, but for a corporate vehicle EUR 12,000 is recommended. At least one manager (gérant) is required; managers may be natural persons or legal entities. Companies whose shares are held by non-EU/non-EEA residents must deposit the full minimum capital at a Luxembourg bank and produce an attestation from that bank within 3 months of incorporation. The trade registry number (RCS number) is issued immediately after notarial deed and must appear on all invoices and contracts. The business activities of 3D game art outsourcing (ISIC 7490, NAICS 541430) require no statutory license in Luxembourg; however, registration with the Joint Social Security Centre (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale) and the RCSL must be completed within 8 days after incorporation. Any commercial activity that targets consumers in EU member states is subject to the EU Consumer Sales and Guarantees Directive and local distance-selling regulations, but B2B outsourcing under contract is generally exempt from consumer-law obligations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended — SARL regime Articles 180-1 to 180-28; implemented with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Grand-Ducal Regulations thereunder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Ministry of Justice; electronic submission via the e-RCS portal and myguichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) executed before a Luxembourg notary; the RCS Single Registration Form (formulaire unique) is lodged electronically by the notary; publication in the official gazette RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and fully paid share capital of EUR 12,000 (Article 180-2 of the Companies Law); cash contributions must be deposited on a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the SARL en formation with a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution, and the bank's blockage certificate is remitted to the notary; contributions in kind require a valuation report by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé (statutory auditor); the company must also build a legal reserve of 5% of annual net profits until the reserve equals 10% of the subscribed capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions presented to this meeting are hereby accepted; the issued share capital of EUR 12,000 having been fully subscribed and paid up in cash to the company's blocked account. RESOLVED, that the registered office located at [street], L-[postal code] Luxembourg, is hereby formally adopted. RESOLVED, that [Full Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) of the company, with unlimited power to bind the company in all dealings, and [Full Name] is appointed as joint signatory for banking matters. RESOLVED, that the manager is authorized to effect the RCS registration, publication in the RESA, VAT and social security registrations, and to complete all post-incorporation filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability search and optional reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — public RCS database and myguichet.lu portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS electronic register to verify that the proposed name is unique and not misleading. If desired, file a name reservation through the myguichet.lu portal, then incorporate the reserved name verbatim in the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (one or more distinctive words, not contrary to public order)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags confusion or similarity with an existing trademark or company, resubmit with an amended name. There is no penalty; a new search and reservation can be lodged immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked escrow account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution — corporate banking desk (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas, Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, or Spuerkeess)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a compte bloqué in the name of the 'SARL en formation'; deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital in cash; complete the bank's AML/KYC checks on each shareholder and beneficial owner; instruct the bank to issue the blockage certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Passports of all shareholders and intended managers
Curriculum vitae / professional profile of each shareholder and manager
Source of funds and source of wealth declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, supply notarized source-of-wealth documentation and professional references. If blocked, choose an alternative EEA credit institution and transfer the same blockage mandate without losing formation priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public — Chamber of Notaries of Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires) — notaries practising in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the draft statutes and the bank blockage certificate to the chosen notary. The notary verifies the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, the share subscriptions, the registered office, and the first manager appointments. The deed is read and signed by all subscribers (or by their attorneys-in-fact). The notary then files the electronic Single Registration Form with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all subscribers and managers
Letter of consent or lease from the owner of the registered office
Power of attorney if a subscriber is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the RCS requires a rectification of the purpose or the name, execute a supplementary notarial deed (acte rectificatif) prior to registration; no prejudice to the formation timeline if the amendment is filed within the same diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon notarial execution, the notary submits the deed and the RCS Single Registration Form electronically. The RCS assigns the unique RCS registration number, and the extract is published in the RESA official gazette. Legal personality vests as from RESA publication; afterwards download the certificate of registration and the official entity extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS suspends the file for missing or illegible attachments, resubmit the corrected set through the notary within fifteen days; priority is preserved and the statutory incorporation date is updated to the corrected filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security, and beneficial owner registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) via myguichet.lu; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) at the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS number is active, apply online for the corporate VAT number and the business-establishment declaration with the AEDT; register as employer with the CCSS prior to hiring; file the RBE beneficial-owner declaration within the legal deadline; open the operating corporate bank account and notify the AEDT of the new account.
required_dossiers: Passports of managers and ultimate beneficial owners
Statement of projected services and turnover for VAT classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is delayed, request expedition at the AEDT single desk; if CCSS reports a late registration, submit an explanatory letter to avoid penalties; RBE declarations can be amended in the RBE portal at any time upon a material change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation corporate, municipal, and workplace compliance setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes; municipal administration (Administration Communale) of the registered-office commune; Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Fulfil the registered-office duty by keeping the statutory minute book, share register, and accounting records at the Luxembourg address. Confirm with the municipal authorities that the premises are zoned for office/administration. Arrange for the annual fire-safety inspection, occupational health assessment, and employer OSH registration with the ITM before the first employee starts. Provide the appointed tax advisor with the incorporation file for corporate income tax, net-wealth tax, and VAT compliance calendar.
required_dossiers: Lease or tenancy agreement for the registered office
Draft employment contracts and OSH risk assessment
Annual accounts and eCDF filing appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal zoning department objects to office use, apply for the applicable planning derogation or relocate within the same commune; if the ITM requires corrective measures, implement them immediately and obtain re-inspection before occupation and staffing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 7490 (3D game-art outsourcing studio) is an office-based professional service in Luxembourg; no industrial licence or manufacturing permit is issued for this activity. The Ministry of the Economy (Service des autorisations d'établissement) would only intervene if the company expanded into regulated crafts or commercial retail.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no operating permit under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to crafts, commerce, and liberal professions applies to non-regulated BPO creative services; the company only needs RCS business registration, municipal commercial occupancy clearance, and ordinary tax/social registrations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environment Agency of Luxembourg) — Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-classified office studio under the Law of 1 August 2018 on environmental permits; no full EIA, prior environmental authorisation, or declaration is triggered for ISIC 7490 creative outsourcing activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions arise; sanitary wastewater discharges into the municipal sewer network must comply with municipal bye-laws; electronic equipment disposal and e-waste must meet the EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and the Luxembourg Waste Law of 21 March 2012; office HVAC and lighting should satisfy applicable energy-performance and refrigerant-control requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGI) confirming adequate fire extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke detectors and evacuation signage; structural load and electrical installation verification for general office occupancy; occupational health and safety compliance supervised by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code, with an OSH risk assessment completed before employees commence work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - the Luxembourg Inland Revenue - for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, solidarity surcharge and withholding taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - for VAT and registration duties. Principal e-portals: MyGuichet.lu (national e-administration gateway), impotsdirects.public.lu (ACD secure filing), the AEDT eTVA portal for VAT returns, and the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) for corporate registration data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL obtains its tax identity through the notarial incorporation flow: (1) the civil-law notary deposits the incorporation deed and statutory documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), which assigns the 13-digit national identification number (matricule / RCS number), publishes the legal notice, and transmits the registration file to the Administration des Contributions Directes; (2) the ACD automatically creates the resident company's direct-tax dossier (numéro de dossier) - no separate TIN application is required for a Luxembourg-resident SARL, and all direct-tax correspondence thereafter uses the matricule as the domestic TIN; (3) for VAT, the SARL must file Form 640 (Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu or in writing, disclosing business activity codes (ISIC 7490 professional B2B services), estimated annual turnover and bank details, after which the AEDT issues the LU VAT number and determines the eTVA filing cycle (monthly or quarterly); (4) a non-established foreign service supplier (one without a Luxembourg registered office) must additionally appoint a tax representative approved by the AEDT before obtaining VAT registration. Normal processing time is 2 to 4 weeks; no filing fee is charged for TIN or VAT-number issuance, although notary and RCS registration costs apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg law; every Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) is necessarily an opaque, entity-level-taxed corporate taxpayer. Available election-type mechanisms include: (i) advance tax ruling (agrément fiscal) from the ACD under coordinated circular L.I.R. 29/2014, which can confirm the participation exemption (Art. 166 L.I.R.), the SPF (Société de Participations Financières) regime (Art. 166bis L.I.R.), or the arm's-length character of cross-border cost-plus outsourcing arrangements; (ii) optional fiscal unity (intégration fiscale, Art. 164bis L.I.R.) allowing a Luxembourg parent and its 95%-or-more-owned Luxembourg subsidiaries to consolidate for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, requiring a joint election within the statutory deadline; (iii) election of the IP box regime (Art. 50ter L.I.R.) giving an 80% exemption of net qualifying intellectual-property income; and (iv) in VAT, election between national AEDT registration and the EU OSS regime for qualifying cross-border B2C supplies. ATAD-aligned anti-hybrid provisions apply mandatorily and cannot be disapprovided; they deny deductions where a foreign jurisdiction classifies the SARL as transparent while Luxembourg treats it as opaque.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and responsible for balance-of-payments statistics and payment system oversight; prudential supervision of credit institutions and EMIs is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Law of 5 April 1993.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg on both current and capital account pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and the dismantling of all Luxembourg exchange-control mechanism by the Grand-Ducal Decree of 1995. No prior administrative authorisation (e.g., BCL or Ministry of Finance approval) is required for opening foreign-currency accounts, borrowing abroad, effecting external payments, or remitting profits. Dividend repatriation is subject only to the standard 15% domestic withholding tax (reduced under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, Luxembourg double-tax treaties, or the participation-exemption regime if the shareholder is an EU/associated company), with no FX or capital-control impediment. Anti-money-laundering and economic-sanctions screening are the only de facto constraints on payment flows, and the BCL requires statistical BOP reporting for non-resident flows above threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes zero statutory surrender ratios, zero mandatory conversion timelines, and no obligation to repatriate export proceeds to any designated account. Hard-currency receivables from non-resident 3D art clients may be retained indefinitely in either EUR or foreign-currency bank accounts wherever the bank permits. The only administrative duty is the statistical declaration of non-resident payments to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes, which the onboarding bank performs automatically on the basis of transaction purpose codes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. A CSSF-licensed or EEA-passported e-money institution (EMI) or payment institution (PI) can legally provide a Luxembourg IBAN, inbound payment collection, and corporate cards, which is adequate for a receivables float. However, EMIs cannot provide primary treasury services such as EUR/USD FX credit lines, commercial letters of credit, short-term lending, or cash pooling; they are also exposed to lower counterparty treatment for settlement of large milestone invoices. An offshore (third-country) EMI has no standalone legal standing to operate a payment account for a Luxembourg SARL unless it acts through an EU-licensed partner. Recommended usage: secondary collection rail for PayPal-derived flows and micro-contractor payouts, never the sole treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote onboarding is legally possible under Luxembourg's AML law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 19/716 when the identification is performed via certified video-identification or a qualified electronic signature (eIDAS). In practice, most Tier-1 banks will accept remote opening only if at least one appointed manager or a registered third-country agent (e.g., a fiduciary or notary) physically signs the account mandate at the bank head office; alternatives include apostilled powers of attorney and the electronic signing of the compliance questionnaire. Low-risk creative-services entities (ISIC 7490) are normally eligible for accelerated onboarding without a physical interview once the UBO is validated against the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crediting of the SARL's statutory minimum capital of EUR 12,000 from a private personal account of the UBO or from a foreign bank in a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement, together with unexplained source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified RBE extract and shareholders' register; notarised incorporation deed and RCS certificate; 6–12 months of UBO bank statements; tax returns and payslips/consulting agreements evidencing accumulated savings; signed source-of-wealth statement; and if inherited, the probate or inheritance deed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indications of a letterbox or low-substance structure: registered office at a virtual-service provider address, no local director, no payroll, and no demonstrable commercial activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance package: physical office or co-working lease in Luxembourg, Luxembourg social-security (CNPF) and payroll attestations, board minutes and an annual substance matrix demonstrating real business decisions in-country, signed game-development contracts with named publishers, a 24-month business plan, and 3D portfolio/references evidencing an actual operating studio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Flows originating from crypto-linked game revenues, 'revenue-share' sweep payments, or unbacked PayPal accumulations with no underlying contracts to named counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full payment profiling: list of all expected customers with corporate identifiers/LEI, invoice-file matching the bank statement, signed master service agreements, PayPal merchant dashboard export, utilisation of standard royalty indexing, and a signed compliance declaration that no transactions with crypto-service providers will be routed through the account without prior written bank consent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial equity: shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 to the dedicated Capital Escrow Account at the primary Tier-1 bank; unambiguously reference the SARL's full legal name and RCS number in Field 50 of the MT103, and insert in Field 70 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION / BPM6 Lin.2.1 DIRECT INVESTMENT / RCS B...' so that the bank allocates the flow to the direct-investment segment of the BCL balance-of-payments return. Intercompany loans and shareholder advances: use MT103 with 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN / BPM6 Lin.2.2.2 / DEBT SECURITY' and a signed intercompany loan agreement, attaching the invoice of the contribution to the annual accounts; the bank will not process the disbursement before the notarised deed is registered with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, and the escrow account is formally released. All non-EUR inbound wires must be pre-advised to the treasury desk to avoid rejection based on restricted-country lines, and each credit must match the purpose code exactly to avoid a BOP suspension.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is the currency-agile default for EUR payments to EU freelance designers, art contractors, servers, licensing agencies, and tax administrations, settled in one business day at no cost. SWIFT MT103 is mandatory for USD/GBP/JPY disbursements to non-EEA game publishers and subcontractors; every outgoing message must carry the beneficiary invoice number and the applicable tax reference to remain compliant with Luxembourg transfer-pricing documentation. Commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) are available for milestone-gated work to unvetted first-time publishers, protecting against non-payment upon delivery of token-sculpture tiers. PayPal business payout (Bulk API) is retained solely as a residual rail for micro-incentive payments under the PSD2 merchant contract, provided invoices are matched to the settlement date and cannot carry the SARL's treasury surplus.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC EUR/USD FX Forwards executed under ISDA 2002 or a Luxembourg Master Agreement, permitted for hedging invoiced and probable 3D art receivables up to 12 months
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing EUR/USD or EUR/GBP strictly for route-to-market collections from restricted-currency jurisdictions, denominated in EUR settlement
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to convert USD milestone income into a fixed-rate EUR liability profile of the SARL for the full contract duration
European-style FX Options (call/put on EUR/USD) used as insurance for large single publisher milestones, with premiums expensed as hedging costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eJustice.lu filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the annual general meeting and in all cases no later than 7 months after the balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year SARL, approval by 30 June and RCS filing by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder from the register; persistent default enables the Public Prosecutor to seek a court order compelling filing under a daily penalty payment (astreinte); repeated non-filing is grounds for judicial strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (confirmation annuelle du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) sub-register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per 12-month period and no later than the annual anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; qualifying share transfers must be reported to the RBE within one month of the transfer and before the annual confirmation snapshot is taken
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning followed by fines under the UBO law (up to EUR 5,000) and possible criminal sanctions for deliberate misdeclaration; continued non-compliance may lead to LBR enforcement and RCS strike-off measures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé applies where the SARL exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce above 50. Audit may also be triggered by shareholders holding at least 10% of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; EU-IFRS is permitted where expressly authorized by law or the articles of association and is mandatory for public-interest entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must review and confirm its RBE declaration at least once per year through the LBR online portal; the confirmation is rendered on the anniversary of the last RBE registration. Any share transfer creating or changing a qualifying beneficial ownership interest must first be recorded in the register of members and then reported to the RBE within one month. The annual confirmation therefore reconciles the register of members, the RBE declaration, and the minutes recording share transfers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,400 – 4,500 per year for registered office, registered agent and basic corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 8,500 per year when compulsory audit thresholds are exceeded; otherwise no statutory audit fee is budgeted

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined Luxembourg CIT at 17%, solidarity surcharge at 7%, and municipal business tax at 6.75% for Luxembourg City, fiscal year 2024/2025)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption on qualifying net IP income (IP box) producing an approximate 5.0% effective tax rate; notional interest deduction for new equity; R&D tax credit and investment reserve can reduce the effective CIT rate to below 24.94% for qualifying activity; no net wealth tax for assets below EUR 500,000 after specific carryforward of unused NWT allowance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 400 (Déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et de l'impôt commercial communal) filed through the Luxembourg e-file portal 'MyGuichet.lu / eTVA' or through a certified tax advisor; separate Form 470 for net wealth tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; advance CIT/MBT instalments are paid quarterly during the fiscal year; the final reconciliation return is filed once per fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year accounts, the return must be filed by 31 May of the following year; for off-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is the last day of the fifth month following the accounting closing date; extensions may be granted by the Administration des contributions directes on written request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: company name, FISC number, legal form SARL, registered office, accounting reference period, tax inspector competent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only for the Luxembourg-resident SARL. Do not report non-resident shareholders as taxpayers unless the non-resident company has a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) or place of effective management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance-sheet net profit or loss before tax per Luxembourg GAAP, reconciled to financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL is owned collectively by non-residents, still report the full Luxembourg taxable result. No consolidation entries may be made for foreign parent accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs: non-deductible expenses, excessive management fees, disguised profit distributions, penalties, payments to tax-haven entities without economic substance, 50% of certain IP-related financing expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related suppliers are not automatically taxable; add-back is required if the payment is disproportionate or lacks substance under Art. 56bis LIR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions: participation exemption dividends, IP box net income exemption, notional interest deduction, R&D incentives, tax-exempt income from foreign PEs relying on treaty relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder with no Luxembourg PE cannot claim these deductions on the SARL return; the SARL alone computes the taxable basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset: enter the amount of prior tax losses actually used against the current-year taxable base before applying the 5-year limitation schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a foreign parent has acquired the SARL in a taxable restructuring, verify that the 25%-change-of-ownership anti-abuse loss forfeiture rule does not invalidate the carried-forward losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT taxable base and municipal business tax base after tax adjustments and loss offset; allocate the base between the State and the municipality of the registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a SARL that is centrally managed and controlled abroad, the tax authorities may treat the Luxembourg seat as a deemed PE; in that case non-resident direct management staff must be included in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: CIT at 17%, solidarity surcharge of 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax at the applicable municipal rate (6.75% in Luxembourg City), with credits for prepayments, dividend WHT and foreign tax credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only when a Luxembourg-resident SARL receives foreign-source income; non-resident shareholders may not file these boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable after advance payments, plus net wealth tax instalments and reminder of statutory interest and penalty computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the shareholder invokes a DTA on inbound dividends paid by the SARL, that refund/reduction claim is made by the shareholder via Form 22, not on this line.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a taxation d'office (ex officio assessment) and a late-filing surcharge usually capped at 10% of the assessed CIT/MBT; late payments attract monthly interest of approximately 0.6% on the outstanding amount; deliberate non-filing or false declarations expose the company to criminal liability and fines up to EUR 250,000 under Art. 153 LIR.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions by a resident SARL; may be reduced to 0% or treaty rate for qualifying non-resident shareholders)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner shareholder must submit Form 22 (demande en réduction / restitution de la retenue à la source) to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD). Attach: (i) valid certificate of fiscal residence (TRC) issued by the state of residence for the relevant calendar year; (ii) declaration of beneficial ownership; (iii) shareholding certificate, including acquisition date and participation percentage; (iv) evidence of the 12-month holding period if relying on the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; and (v) payment/bank confirmation of the dividend. The ACD may grant relief at source if the payer has advance clearance; otherwise the claim is processed and repaid with interest after verification. For EU resident corporate parents holding at least 10% for 12 months, the exemption is applied at source automatically upon presentation of the TRC and a sworn statement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic withholding on payments to non-resident companies without a Luxembourg PE; 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for associated EU companies; DTA rates generally 0%–10%. Interest: 0% domestic withholding on ordinary cross-border interest to non-residents without a Luxembourg PE; profits-participating interest/bonds remain subject to 15%; DTA rates generally 0%–10% (0% for EU associated companies).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where aggregate cross-border controlled transactions exceed EUR 1.5 million in a fiscal year; Master File is required where the consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750 million; below these thresholds a concise arm’s-length pricing policy and intercompany agreement record must nevertheless be contemporaneously available.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Luxembourg does not apply a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation, but under Art. 56 LIR substance-over-form, the ATAD general anti-abuse rule, the Luxembourg tax residence certificate policy and the 2019 tax-administration circular on factual substance, the SARL must show real economic presence: physical office, resident staff or service providers performing actual 3D-art work, local bank account, board decisions in Luxembourg, and commercial contracts directing risk and functions. Transactional substance is tested through a full functional analysis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of outsourced 3D-art contract revenue; using PayPal or offshore accounts not disclosed to the Luxembourg tax authorities; issuing invoices for non-existent subcontractors; inflating artist payroll costs; destroying accounting books
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment with an extended 10-year tax limitation; penalty surcharge up to 200% of evaded CIT, MBT, and net wealth tax; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under Art. 153 LIR and Art. 402 of the Criminal Code; monthly late-payment interest at 0.6% on evaded amounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly participate in concealment are subject to piercing of the corporate veil: joint and several civil restitution of the evaded taxes, travel bans, seizure of personal bank accounts, disqualification from directing a Luxembourg company for up to 10 years, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SARL solely as a flow-through invoice platform without dedicated office, employees, business contracts, client communication or management substance; routing gross proceeds through a letter-box parent and retaining no taxable margin; holding IP or bank accounts without any Luxembourg decision-making
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the Luxembourg tax residence certificate; refusal of treaty benefits and EU directive exemptions; complete disregard of the entity under substance-over-form; reallocation of income to the true beneficial owner; penalty of 100% on under-assessed tax; interest and compulsory liquidation exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for all taxes re-assessed after the entity is disregarded; travel bans and asset freezes are issued in international fraud investigations; imprisonment for up to 3 years where the artificial structure is used to evade tax or money launder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No arm’s-length benchmarking for 3D-art contracts; paying management fees equal to nearly all operating profit to a non-resident shareholder; charging below-margin rates to an offshore affiliate while using Luxembourg costs; nonexistent or contradictory intercompany agreements; refusing to produce a Local File when controlled transactions exceed EUR 1.5 million
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under Art. 56bis LIR reallocating the taxable income to the arm’s-length standard; compensating assessment against the SARL; equalization of hidden distributions; 100% penalty for intentional mispricing; monthly interest; deemed dividend withholding tax of 15% on the adjusted excess
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally approve artificial pricing or sign inflated invoices become jointly liable for the company’s tax deficiencies; the corporate veil is pierced where the shareholder and director are identical; civil restitution, prohibition from management, travel restrictions, and imprisonment for up to 3 years in case of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting anonymous PayPal or wire payments for 3D-art projects without KYC; failing to identify the beneficial owner of a client or subcontractor; suppressing transactions to stay below AML thresholds; refusing cooperation with suspicious transaction reporting; making bulk cash withdrawals to pay artists
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 per breach under the amended Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT; confiscation of funds; criminal money-laundering sanctions including fines up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; revocation of professional authorisations; inclusion in regulatory blacklists
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for failures in the AML/CFT compliance function of the SARL; they face civil damages, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, criminal imprisonment up to 5 years, and permanent disqualification from holding office in Luxembourg financial or commercial enterprises.
